question:
Who among the following was the Vakil under the reign of Mughal Emperor Akbar, who received the title of Khan-i-Khanan ?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Mulla do-Piyaza
Birbal
Raja Todar Mal
Bairam Khan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bairam Khan

Explanation:
Bairam Khan was a prominent advisor and military commander during the reign of Mughal Emperor Akbar. He held the title of 'Khan-i-Khanan', one of the highest military and administrative ranks in the Mughal court. Bairam Khan served as Akbar's regent during his childhood and played a crucial role in stabilizing the Mughal Empire after Humayun's death. He assisted Akbar in defeating Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556), which consolidated Mughal power.

Extra Facts:
Bairam Khan was a Shia Muslim and contributed significantly in the early years of Akbar's reign. However, Akbar later sent him to Mecca for Hajj, where he was assassinated. His son, Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, became a famous poet and commander in Akbar's court.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन मुगल सम्राट अकबर के शासनकाल में वकील था, जिसे खान-ए-खाना की उपाधि प्राप्त थी?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options_hi: मुल्ला दो-प्याजा
बीरबल
राजा टोडरमल
बैरम खान
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है बैरम खान

Explanation:
बैरम खान मुगल सम्राट अकबर के शासनकाल में एक प्रमुख सलाहकार और सेनापति थे। उन्हें 'खान-ए-खाना' की उपाधि प्राप्त थी, जो मुगल दरबार में सर्वोच्च सैन्य और प्रशासनिक पदों में से एक थी। बैरम खान ने अकबर के बचपन में उनके संरक्षक के रूप में कार्य किया और हुमायूँ की मृत्यु के बाद मुगल साम्राज्य को स्थिर करने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। उन्होंने पानीपत की दूसरी लड़ाई (1556) में हेमू को हराने में अकबर की मदद की, जिससे मुगल सत्ता को मजबूती मिली।

Extra Facts:
बैरम खान एक शिया मुस्लिम थे और उन्होंने अकबर के शासनकाल के प्रारंभिक वर्षों में महत्वपूर्ण योगदान दिया। हालांकि, बाद में अकबर ने उन्हें हज के लिए मक्का भेज दिया, जहाँ उनकी हत्या कर दी गई। उनके बेटे अब्दुल रहीम खान-ए-खाना भी एक प्रसिद्ध कवि और सेनापति बने और अकबर के दरबार में उच्च पद पर आसीन रहे।

question:
Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: Mirza Mohammad Qasim : Shahjahan Nama
Gulbadan Begum : Humayun Nama
Abul Fazl : Akbarnama
Abdul Hamid Lahori : Padshahnama
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mirza Mohammad Qasim : Shahjahan Nama

Explanation:
Mirza Mohammad Qasim wrote 'Alamgirnama', not 'Shahjahan Nama'. The 'Shahjahan Nama' was written by Inayat Khan, which describes the reign of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. All other pairs are correctly matched: Gulbadan Begum wrote 'Humayun Nama', based on Humayun's life; Abul Fazl wrote 'Akbarnama', a detailed history of Akbar's reign; and Abdul Hamid Lahori wrote 'Padshahnama', the official chronicle of Shah Jahan's reign.

Extra Facts:
Mughal historiography was dominated by the Persian language. The 'Akbarnama' is considered the most important text of Mughal history, containing detailed information about Akbar's reign. Gulbadan Begum, Humayun's sister, authored 'Humayun Nama', a unique document in Mughal history as it was written by a woman.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा युग्म गलत तरीके से मेल खाता है?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options_hi: मिर्ज़ा मोहम्मद कासिम : शाहजहाँहां नामा
गुलबदन बेगम : हुमायूं नामा
अबुल फजल : अकबरनामा
अब्दुल हमीद लाहौरी : पदशाहनामा
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है मिर्ज़ा मोहम्मद कासिम : शाहजहाँनामा

Explanation:
मिर्ज़ा मोहम्मद कासिम ने 'आलमगीरनामा' लिखा था, न कि 'शाहजहाँनामा'। 'शाहजहाँनामा' इनायत खान द्वारा लिखा गया था, जो मुगल सम्राट शाहजहाँ के शासनकाल का विवरण देता है। अन्य सभी युग्म सही हैं: गुलबदन बेगम ने 'हुमायूँनामा' लिखा, जो हुमायूँ के जीवन पर आधारित है; अबुल फजल ने 'अकबरनामा' लिखा, जो अकबर के शासनकाल का विस्तृत इतिहास है; और अब्दुल हमीद लाहौरी ने 'पादशाहनामा' लिखा, जो शाहजहाँ के शासनकाल का आधिकारिक इतिहास है।

Extra Facts:
मुगलकालीन इतिहासलेखन में फारसी भाषा का प्रभुत्व था। अकबरनामा को मुगल इतिहास का सबसे महत्वपूर्ण ग्रंथ माना जाता है, जिसमें अकबर के शासनकाल की विस्तृत जानकारी है। गुलबदन बेगम, हुमायूँ की बहन थीं और उनका 'हुमायूँनामा' मुगल इतिहास में एक अनूठा दस्तावेज है, क्योंकि यह एक महिला द्वारा लिखा गया था।

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :

☛ बाबर - 'बाबरनामा' (तुजुक-ए-बाबरी) के लेखक (मुगल साम्राज्य के संस्थापक)

question:
Which of the following pairs of ‘Ruler – Ruling period’ is correctly matched?
I. Sher Shah Suri – 1540-1545
II. Akbar – 1556-1605

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Neither I nor II
Only II
Only I
Both I and II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is [Both I and II]

Explanation:
Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun in 1540 and ruled until 1545. He established an efficient administrative system, including the 'Rupiya' and 'Dam' currency, construction of the Grand Trunk Road, and land revenue reforms (Ryotwari System).

Akbar (1556-1605) ascended the throne at 13 and expanded the Mughal Empire. He introduced Din-i-Ilahi, the Mansabdari System, and the policy of Sulh-e-Kul.

Extra Facts:

question:
Who among the following Mughal Emperors had assumed the title of Padshah?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Jahangir
Babur
Humayun
Akbar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Babur

Explanation:
Babur was the first Mughal emperor to assume the title of 'Padshah'. He founded the Mughal Empire in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526). The term 'Padshah' is a Persian title meaning 'Great Emperor' or 'King of Kings'. Babur used this title to assert his supreme authority and imperial ambitions. He also mentioned this in his autobiography, 'Baburnama'.

Extra Facts:
Babur hailed from the Fergana Valley in Central Asia and was a descendant of Timur. He laid the foundation of the Mughal rule in India, which was later consolidated by his grandson Akbar. Babur fought several significant battles, including the Battle of Khanwa (1527) and the Battle of Ghaghra (1529).

निम्नलिखित मुगल सम्राटों में से किसने पादशाह की उपाधि धारण की थी?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: जहाँगीर
बाबर
हुमायूँ
अकबर
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है बाबर

Explanation:
बाबर ने पहले मुगल सम्राट के रूप में 'पादशाह' की उपाधि धारण की थी। उसने 1526 में पानीपत की पहली लड़ाई में इब्राहिम लोदी को हराकर भारत में मुगल साम्राज्य की स्थापना की। 'पादशाह' एक फारसी शब्द है जिसका अर्थ 'महान सम्राट' या 'राजाओं का राजा' होता है। बाबर ने इस उपाधि का उपयोग अपनी सर्वोच्चता और साम्राज्यवादी महत्वाकांक्षा को दर्शाने के लिए किया। उसने अपनी आत्मकथा 'बाबरनामा' में भी इसका उल्लेख किया है।

Extra Facts:
बाबर मध्य एशिया के फरगना घाटी से था और तैमूर वंश से संबंधित था। उसने भारत में मुगल शासन की नींव रखी, जिसे उसके पोते अकबर ने और मजबूत किया। बाबर ने अपने शासनकाल में कई महत्वपूर्ण युद्ध लड़े, जिनमें खानवा का युद्ध (1527) और घाघरा का युद्ध (1529) प्रमुख हैं।

question:
_______, a Muslim saint, lived at the place where Fatehpur Sikri was built.

[RRB ALP CBT]
options: Nizamuddin Auliya
Nasiruddin Chiragh Dehlavi
Sheikh Salim Chisti
Baba Fakruddin
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sheikh Salim Chisti

Explanation:
Fatehpur Sikri was built by the Mughal emperor Akbar. This site was located near the cave of the famous Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chisti. Akbar was blessed with a son (Jahangir) as prophesied by the saint, after which he established Fatehpur Sikri at this very location. The tomb of Sheikh Salim Chisti still stands in Fatehpur Sikri and is an important religious site.

Extra Facts:
Fatehpur Sikri is also called the 'City of Victory' and served as the Mughal capital from 1571 to 1585. It was constructed using red sandstone and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Akbar built iconic structures here, including the Diwan-i-Khas, Buland Darwaza, and Jodha Bai’s Palace.

question_hi:
______, एक मुस्लिम संत थे, जो उस जगह पर रहते थे जहाँ फतेहपुर सीकरी का निर्माण किया गया था।

[RRB ALP CBT]
options_hi: निजामुद्दीन औलिया
नसीरुद्दीन चिराग देहलवी
शेख सलीम चिश्ती
बाबा फखरुद्दीन
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है शेख सलीम चिश्ती

Explanation:
फतेहपुर सीकरी का निर्माण मुग़ल बादशाह अकबर ने करवाया था। यह स्थान उस समय प्रसिद्ध सूफ़ी संत शेख सलीम चिश्ती की गुफा के पास स्थित था। अकबर को संत की भविष्यवाणी के अनुसार एक पुत्र (जहाँगीर) की प्राप्ति हुई थी, जिसके बाद उन्होंने इसी स्थान पर फतेहपुर सीकरी बसाया। शेख सलीम चिश्ती का मकबरा आज भी फतेहपुर सीकरी में मौजूद है और यह एक महत्वपूर्ण धार्मिक स्थल है।

Extra Facts:

question:
Which Mughal Emperor has attempted to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora?

[SSC MTS 2022]

Humayun
Shah Jahan
Babur
solution:

Explanation:
Aurangzeb attempted to destroy the Kailash Temple at Ellora. He was a staunch Sunni Muslim ruler who adopted a policy of demolishing Hindu temples. He damaged several prominent temples, including the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and the Keshav Dev Temple in Mathura. However, the Kailash Temple, being carved out of a single massive rock, could not be completely destroyed. This act reflects Aurangzeb's religious intolerance and his attitude towards Hindu culture.

Extra Facts:
The Kailash Temple was built by Rashtrakuta King Krishna I (8th century). It is the world's largest monolithic temple, sculpted from a single rock. During Aurangzeb's reign, the Mughal Empire was at its peak in terms of territorial expansion, but his religious policies led to growing discontent within the empire.

Akbar's army was led by Man Singh and Asaf Khan. In this battle, the Mughal forces defeated Maharana Pratap, but they could never fully subjugate him. Maharana Pratap continued his struggle against the Mughals using guerrilla warfare tactics. This battle is considered a symbol of Rajput valor and pride in Indian history.

Extra Facts:
The Battle of Haldighati is also known as the 'Struggle for Mewar's Independence'. Maharana Pratap's famous horse, 'Chetak', played a crucial role in this battle and attained martyrdom while saving his master. Akbar launched multiple invasions to capture Mewar, but Maharana Pratap never accepted his subjugation.

बाबर ने भारत में मुगल साम्राज्य की नींव रखी और उसकी आत्मकथा 'बाबरनामा' मध्यकालीन इतिहास का एक महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत है। उसने तुलुगमा युद्ध नीति और तोपखाने का प्रभावी उपयोग करके अपनी सेना को मजबूत बनाया। उसकी मृत्यु 1530 में हुई, और उसके बाद उसका पुत्र हुमायूँ सिंहासन पर बैठा।

question:
Who built the Pathar Ki Masjid in Patna, Bihar?

[SSC CHSL 2022]

Alauddin Khilji
solution:

Explanation:
The Pathar Ki Masjid was built by Parwez Shah, the eldest son of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. Located in Patna, Bihar, this mosque was constructed in the 17th century using red sandstone, which gives it the name 'Pathar Ki Masjid' (Stone Mosque). The mosque is an excellent example of Mughal architecture and holds significant religious importance for Muslims.

Extra Facts:
Parwez Shah, whose full name was Sultan Muhammad Parwez, was the eldest son of Shah Jahan. He was appointed as the Subedar (governor) of Bengal and Bihar. During the Mughal era, Patna was a major trade and cultural hub. Apart from this mosque, Parwez Shah commissioned several other structures that stand as historical landmarks today.

question:
Ain-i Akbari, a document on life of Mughal ruler Akbar does not contain information about _________

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Revenues
Ancestors
Army
Administration
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ancestors

Explanation:
The Ain-i Akbari, written by Abul Fazl, is a significant historical document that details various aspects of Mughal Emperor Akbar's reign (1556-1605 CE). It is the third volume of the Akbarnama and contains extensive information on revenues, army, administration, socio-economic conditions, arts, and culture. However, it does not provide detailed information about Akbar's ancestors. The document primarily focuses on the administrative and cultural aspects of Akbar's rule.

Extra Facts:
Abul Fazl was one of Akbar's 'Nine Jewels' (Navratnas) and meticulously recorded his reign. The Ain-i Akbari includes details of the Mughal land revenue system (e.g., Zabti system), military organization (Mansabdari system), and descriptions of various provinces. It is a key source for understanding the socio-economic history of the Mughal era.

question:
In 1526, ______ was defeated by Babur at Panipat.

[SSC MTS ]

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ibrahim Lodi

Explanation:
The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was a pivotal event in Indian history where Mughal Emperor Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, establishing the Mughal Empire in India. The battle was fought on 21 April 1526. Babur effectively used gunpowder artillery and the Tulughma tactic, while Ibrahim Lodi relied on traditional warfare methods. This battle marked the end of the Lodi Dynasty and the beginning of the Mughal Empire.

Extra Facts:
Ibrahim Lodi (1517-1526) was the last ruler of the Lodi Dynasty. His reign was marked by conflicts with Afghan nobles, weakening his authority. Babur exploited this and secured a decisive victory at Panipat. After this battle, Delhi and Agra came under Mughal control, ushering in a new era in Indian history.

question:
In which of the following years was the Mughal empire established by Babur?

[SSC CGL 2020]
options: 1699
1578
1526
1634
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1526

Explanation:
Babur established the Mughal Empire in 1526 after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat. This battle marked a significant turning point in Indian history as it ended the Lodi dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate and laid the foundation of Mughal rule in India. Babur, who hailed from the Fergana Valley in Central Asia, claimed descent from Timur and Genghis Khan. He expanded his empire in India and founded the Mughal dynasty, which ruled for nearly 300 years.

Extra Facts:
The First Battle of Panipat (21 April 1526) saw Babur effectively using artillery and the 'Tulghuma' warfare strategy, which secured his decisive victory. Babur documented this battle in his autobiography, 'Baburnama', written in Chagatai Turkic. After establishing the Mughal Empire, Babur made Agra his capital.

question:
Sikandra is the final resting place of Emperor ______.

[SSC CGL 2021]
options: Jahangir

Akbar
Humayun
solution:

Explanation:
Sikandra, located near Agra, is the mausoleum of the Mughal Emperor Akbar. Akbar himself initiated the construction of this tomb during his lifetime, but it was completed by his son Jahangir between 1605-1613 CE. This tomb is a magnificent example of Mughal architecture, showcasing a blend of Hindu, Islamic, Jain, and Christian architectural styles. Akbar died in 1605 CE and was buried in this mausoleum.

Extra Facts:
Akbar was the third and greatest ruler of the Mughal Empire, reigning from 1556 to 1605. He adopted a policy of religious tolerance and founded a new religion called Din-i-Ilahi. His court had nine gems (Navratnas), including scholars like Birbal, Todar Mal, and Tansen.

___________administration became the model followed by the great emperor Akbar when he consolidated the Mughal Empire.

[SSC CHSL 2022]

Genghis Khan's

Explanation:
Sher Shah Suri (1540-1545 CE) established an efficient administrative system during his brief reign, which was later adopted by the Mughal emperor Akbar. Sher Shah introduced key reforms like the 'Dahsala System' (land revenue), standardized Rupiya (silver coin), and built the Grand Trunk Road. Akbar refined these systems to consolidate the Mughal Empire. Sher Shah’s emphasis on justice and governance set a benchmark for future rulers.

Extra Facts:
Sher Shah founded the Sur Empire after defeating Humayun. He made Patna his capital and reformed the postal system. His death in 1545 CE (during the siege of Kalinjar Fort) marked the decline of the Sur dynasty. Akbar’s adoption of his policies (e.g., Mansabdari) strengthened Mughal administration.

question:
Tansen, the famous singer of the Mughal era, is associated with which Indian music form?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Carnatic
Thumri
Khayal
Dhrupad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dhrupad

Explanation:
Tansen, one of the 'Navratnas' (Nine Jewels) in Mughal Emperor Akbar's court, was one of the greatest singers in Indian classical music. He was associated with the Dhrupad style, the oldest and most solemn form of Indian classical music. Dhrupad originated from Vedic chants and focuses on devotion and knowledge. Tansen elevated this style and popularized it in the Mughal court. He also composed many new ragas, such as Miyan Ki Malhar and Darbari Kanada, which remain famous today.

Extra Facts:
Tansen was born in Gwalior, and his original name was Ramtanu Pandey. He learned music from his guru, Haridas Swami, a renowned Dhrupad singer. Akbar honored him with the title 'Miyan Tansen'. Legends say his singing could bring rain and light lamps spontaneously, showcasing his divine artistry.

question_hi:
मुगल काल के प्रसिद्ध गायक तानसेन का संबंध किस भारतीय संगीत से है?

Extra Facts:
तानसेन का जन्म ग्वालियर में हुआ था और उनका मूल नाम रामतनु पांडे था। उन्होंने गुरु हरिदास स्वामी से संगीत की शिक्षा ली, जो ध्रुपद के महान गायक थे। अकबर ने उन्हें 'मियाँ तानसेन' की उपाधि दी। तानसेन की कला इतनी उच्च कोटि की थी कि कहा जाता है कि उनके गायन से बादल बरसने लगते थे और दीपक स्वयं जल उठते थे।

question:
In which year did the Mongols under Genghis Khan invade Transoxiana in North-East Iran?

[SSC MTS ]

1208
1213
1205
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1219

Explanation:
Under the leadership of Genghis Khan, the Mongols invaded Transoxiana (modern-day Uzbekistan and Tajikistan) in 1219 CE. This invasion was directed against the Khwarazmian Empire, ruled by Ala ad-Din Muhammad. The immediate cause of the invasion was the Otrar Massacre, where the Khwarazmian governor executed Mongol traders. Genghis Khan retaliated with a massive army, leading to the destruction of the Khwarazmian Empire. This campaign was a significant part of the Mongols' global conquests.

Extra Facts:
Transoxiana is a historical region in Central Asia, located between the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers. The Mongol invasion established their dominance in the region, paving the way for future rulers like Timur (Tamerlane). Genghis Khan's army employed advanced siege tactics and psychological warfare during this campaign.

Her influence during Jahangir's reign was so profound that she was also referred to as 'Shahanshah-e-Nur'.

Extra Facts:
Nur Jahan was born in 1577 in Kandahar (Afghanistan). Her father, Mirza Ghiyas Beg (later known as 'Itimad-ud-Daulah'), was a Persian noble. Nur Jahan entered the Mughal court with her family and gradually gained Jahangir's attention through her intelligence. She patronized art, literature, and architecture and commissioned monuments like the 'Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah' in Agra.

[SSC MTS 2024]

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है मेहरुन्निसा (Mehrunnisa)

Explanation:
मेहरुन्निसा ने 1611 ई. में मुग़ल बादशाह जहाँगीर से विवाह किया और उन्हें 'नूरजहाँ' (दुनिया की रोशनी) की उपाधि प्राप्त हुई। वह एक प्रभावशाली महिला थीं और मुग़ल दरबार में उनका काफ़ी प्रभाव था। नूरजहाँ ने राजनीतिक और प्रशासनिक मामलों में सक्रिय भूमिका निभाई और उन्हें 'बेगम साहिबा' के रूप में भी जाना जाता था। उन्होंने सिक्कों पर अपना नाम खुदवाया और कई महत्वपूर्ण निर्णयों में हिस्सा लिया। जहाँगीर के शासनकाल में उनका प्रभाव इतना बढ़ गया था कि उन्हें 'शहंशाह-ए-नूर' भी कहा जाता था।

Extra Facts:
नूरजहाँ का जन्म 1577 ई. में कंधार (अफ़गानिस्तान) में हुआ था। उनके पिता मिर्ज़ा गयास बेग (जो बाद में 'इतिमाद-उद-दौला' के नाम से प्रसिद्ध हुए) एक फ़ारसी अमीर थे। नूरजहाँ ने अपने परिवार के साथ मुग़ल दरबार में प्रवेश किया और धीरे-धीरे अपनी प्रतिभा से जहाँगीर का ध्यान आकर्षित किया। उन्होंने कला, साहित्य और वास्तुकला को भी प्रोत्साहित किया और आगरा में 'इतिमाद-उद-दौला का मकबरा' जैसी इमारतों का निर्माण करवाया।
